articleTitle: Scattering of a plane electromagnetic wave by a perfectly conducting disk in the high-frequency approximation
publicationTitle: International Seminar. Day on Diffraction '2001. Proceedings (IEEE Cat.No.01EX477)
abstract: A high-frequency asymptotic approach based on Green's formula has been used to develop a unifying framework for scattering of a plane electromagnetic wave of arbitrary incidence from a perfectly conducting planar disk of arbitrary shape with a smooth edge. The method provides asymptotic formulas of uniform geometrical theory of diffraction to describe the scattered field in the near field zone. A particular case of scattering of transverse electric linear polarized wave (TE case) from a disk is considered in comparison with the Kirchhoff approximation. The computer code based on the asymptotic formulas proved to be very fast and quite accurate.

articleTitle: Scattering of electromagnetic waves in a channel with a step-like boundary
publicationTitle: International Seminar. Day on Diffraction '2001. Proceedings (IEEE Cat.No.01EX477)
abstract: An optimization problem for the multichannel electrodynamical systems of energy accumulation is considered. The aim is to achieve a homogeneous electric field of maximum amplitude in the near axis domain. The energy provided in such systems requires the use of a structure of periodic narrow channels with Bragg reflectors. To define the optimal parameters, the model scattering problem with one Bragg reflector is solved. To obtain an approximate solution, the method of discrete sources is developed. A new way of source placement is suggested. To avoid incorrectness of the problem considered, the modification of the classical regularization procedure is applied. A comparison of numerical and analytical solutions is performed.

articleTitle: Diffraction by two ideal strips
publicationTitle: International Seminar. Day on Diffraction '2001. Proceedings (IEEE Cat.No.01EX477)
abstract: The problem of scattering of a plane wave by two ideal strips lying in one plane is studied. The Wiener-Hopf functional equation is formulated and studied. The following results are obtained. (1) The embedding formula is derived. This formula enables one to express the far-field diagram, depending on two variables (the angle of incidence and the angle of scattering) as the combination of 4 functions depending on one variable. (2) The ordinary differential equation with respect to the spectral variable is derived for the components of the far-field diagram. (3) The evolution equation describing the dependence of the far-field diagram on the parameters of the problem (such as the coordinates of the edges of the scatterer) are derived.

articleTitle: Diffraction by dielectric wedge
publicationTitle: International Seminar. Day on Diffraction '2001. Proceedings (IEEE Cat.No.01EX477)
abstract: The scattering of a plane monochromatic wave by a infinite dielectric wedge is discussed for arbitrary direction of incidence. The wave velocities in the interior and exterior of the wedge are distinct. At the boundary of the wedge there is a pair of transmissions conditions. We also impose Meixner's condition at the edge. The wave field should also satisfy the radiation condition at infinity. Here we follow the approach based on Sommerfeld transforms and first applied in scalar problem by Maliuzhinets (1955, 1957, 1958) in his study of diffraction by wedge with impedance boundary conditions. Maliuzhinets reformulated the diffraction problem in the form of functional equations for Sommerfeld transform. Budaev (1995) reduced the diffraction problem for an elastic wedge to two decoupled systems of two functional equations and then to two singular integral equations. The Sommerfeld-Maliuzhinets method is used to represent the field in the interior and exterior regions of the wedge by means of two spectral functions. The original problem is decoupled into two, symmetric and antisymmetric. A pair of functional equations are obtained for these unknown spectral functions.

articleTitle: Spherical-harmonic representation of transient waves produced by sources on a superluminal expanding sphere
publicationTitle: International Seminar. Day on Diffraction '2001. Proceedings (IEEE Cat.No.01EX477)
abstract: The goal of this report is to construct the explicit solutions to the inhomogeneous wave equation in terms of transient spherical harmonics. These solutions describe waves in free space formed by the source distribution on a sphere expanding with a velocity greater than the wavefront velocity. In the particular case we get a description of waves produced by the source distribution on the specific expanding circle that belongs to the sphere, and give the algorithm constructing solutions to the problem of wave formation by a point source moving on a circle. The results obtained allow us to write at once solutions of analogous problems in the case of a sphere expanding with a velocity equal and less than the wavefront velocity. The one-component radial Hertz vector, introduced by Debye (1909) and Bromwich (1919), permit us to apply the scalar wave functions to electromagnetic waves. Solutions of the initial-value problem are constructed with the help of the method described by Manankova (1972).

articleTitle: Limiting absorption principle and the particle current conservation for one-dimensional geometric scattering
publicationTitle: International Seminar. Day on Diffraction '2001. Proceedings (IEEE Cat.No.01EX477)
abstract: Let H/sub 0/ be a self-adjoint operator in R/sup d/ defined by the Laplacian: H/sub 0/=-/spl Delta/.. The expression for d>2 the, Green function G/sub 0/ (x, y; z) of H/sub 0/ (i.e. the integral kernel of the resolvent R/sub 0/(z)=(H /sub 0/-z)/sup -1/) is given. The goal of this paper is to show that at least in the case d/spl les/3 a relation that expresses the particle current conservation for the one-dimensional geometric scattering in R/sup d/. Moreover, this relation is valid and has the same physical sense in the case of the Lobachevsky plane or the three-dimensional Lobachevsky space.

articleTitle: Three wave interaction analysis in the presence of far-reaching correlations of stochastic irregularities
publicationTitle: International Seminar. Day on Diffraction '2001. Proceedings (IEEE Cat.No.01EX477)
abstract: The propagation of wave triplet is investigated in media which is composed of large periodically repeating stochastic pieces. The correlation scale of the nonuniformities is assumed to be small within one period (delta correlation), but there is strong correlation of irregularities at the distance equal to the media period. We have examined the waves properties verses to the multiple of pass of the identical piece. The results obtained demonstrate the substantial dependence of the solutions from the existence of random parameter far-reaching correlations.

articleTitle: Perturbation method in the problem of diffraction of an obliquely incident electromagnetic plane wave by an impedance wedge and the diffraction coefficients
publicationTitle: International Seminar. Day on Diffraction '2001. Proceedings (IEEE Cat.No.01EX477)
abstract: We study the problem of diffraction of an EM plane wave by an impedance wedge. In the general case of oblique incidence the problem was not solved explicitly, however, in some special cases of surface impedances the analytic solution has been obtained. The most natural way to obtain the practically important results for the diffraction coefficient in the general case of skew incidence is to apply the perturbation method. The problem can be solved for the normal incidence and for the grazing to the edge incidence. This enables us to develop the perturbation procedure for the following two cases: for very skew and almost normal incidences.

articleTitle: Restoration of parameters of viscoelastic inhomogeneities by diffraction tomography
publicationTitle: International Seminar. Day on Diffraction '2001. Proceedings (IEEE Cat.No.01EX477)
abstract: Numerical simulation of restoration of parameters of viscoelastic local inhomogeneity (comparable in size with the wavelength) by the diffraction tomography method based upon the first-order Born approximation is considered. The direct problem is solved by the finite difference method.

articleTitle: An edge wave diffraction from a line of curvature jump
publicationTitle: International Seminar. Day on Diffraction '2001. Proceedings (IEEE Cat.No.01EX477)
abstract: The problem of the diffraction of creeping waves on a point of transition of the convex boundary to the straight boundary of a domain is investigated. It is assumed that at the point of jump of curvature, the tangent to the boundary is continuous and it's derivative has a jump.. It is also assumed that that point of jump is situated in the penumbra region. An expression for the edge wave is obtained.

articleTitle: On natural frequencies of the rectangular acoustic resonator with piecewise-homogeneous elastic wall
publicationTitle: International Seminar. Day on Diffraction '2001. Proceedings (IEEE Cat.No.01EX477)
abstract: The problem of natural steady-state vibrations of rectangular resonators with homogeneous elastic walls was considered in numerous publications. Cases of inhomogeneous walls are considered much more rarely. The present research concerns one such case.

articleTitle: Matching of asymptotic models in scattering of acoustic waves by elastic shells
publicationTitle: International Seminar. Day on Diffraction '2001. Proceedings (IEEE Cat.No.01EX477)
abstract: Scattering of stationary acoustic waves by elastic shells is considered. The approximate solution of the problem is synthesized by matching of asymptotic models having the limited ranges of applicability. In the vicinity of zero frequency the Kirchhoff-Love theory of shells or the refined Kirchhoff-Love theory is applied, in the vicinities of thickness resonance frequencies the long-wave high-frequency approximations are utilized and outside these vicinities the flat elastic layer model is applied. It is shown that the mentioned models have overlapping regions. As examples, the problems for scattering of a plane acoustic wave by circular cylindrical and spherical shells are considered. Numerical results of comparison with the relevant exact solution are presented.

articleTitle: The depolarization effect in the problem of diffraction on a grating consisting of thin semi infinite chiral slabs
publicationTitle: International Seminar. Day on Diffraction '2001. Proceedings (IEEE Cat.No.01EX477)
abstract: The diffraction of a normally incident plane wave by a grating consisting of thin semi infinite chiral slabs is considered. The chiral slabs are simulated by the appropriate first-order transition boundary conditions. The problem is simplified by decoupling E/sub z/ and H/sub z/ components via a similarity transformation. Then, the problem is reduced to the scalar Riemann-Hilbert problems and solved in an explicit form. The expansion of the diffracted field in terms of the plane waves is obtained and the depolarization effect is discussed.

articleTitle: Equations of the effective model of a porous block medium
publicationTitle: International Seminar. Day on Diffraction '2001. Proceedings (IEEE Cat.No.01EX477)
abstract: The porous medium consisting of rectangular blocks is considered. In the case of slide contact on interfaces the averaged effective model can be established for this medium. The equations describing wave propagation in this effective model are investigated.

articleTitle: Short-wavelength asymptotics for the low Landau zones of the two-dimensional magnetic Schro/spl uml/dinger operator
publicationTitle: International Seminar. Day on Diffraction '2001. Proceedings (IEEE Cat.No.01EX477)
abstract: We study an asymptotic behavior of the bottom part for the spectrum of the two-dimensional magnetic Schro/spl uml/dinger operator with uniform magnetic and periodic electric fields. Using averaging methods we reduce the corresponding classical problem to a one-dimensional Hamiltonian system on the torus and obtain almost invariant manifolds of the original Hamiltonian. Asymptotics of the spectrum is constructed now by means of the canonical operator with a complex germ.

articleTitle: On nonlinear elastic waves in a circular plate
publicationTitle: International Seminar. Day on Diffraction '2001. Proceedings (IEEE Cat.No.01EX477)
abstract: The problem on longitudinal deformation wave propagation is considered in a homogeneous isotropic non-linear elastic disk, finite in two directions r and /spl phi/, and very thin in z. Depending on small parameter introduction different equations are derived and several exact solutions are obtained.

articleTitle: Mechanical vibrations of freely standing smectic-A films
publicationTitle: International Seminar. Day on Diffraction '2001. Proceedings (IEEE Cat.No.01EX477)
abstract: The time-dependent layer displacement-layer displacement correlation functions are analyzed in a free standing thin smectic-A films with the help of the discrete layer model. The film motions are described using the Chebyshev polynomials of second kind, U/sub n/(x). The dependencies of the eigenmodes on the wave number q/sub /spl perp// were analyzed. For small q/sub /spl perp// one mode is a low frequency acoustic wave and other modes are high frequency optical oscillations. The rather simple expression for the susceptibility matrix and for spectral densities of layer displacement correlation functions were obtained using the Chebyshev polynomials. The obtained results allow one to explain the experimental results on dynamic scattering and diffraction of X-rays in smectic-A films.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic wave excitation by a modulated electron beam injected in an anisotropic plasma channel
publicationTitle: International Seminar. Day on Diffraction '2001. Proceedings (IEEE Cat.No.01EX477)
abstract: A study is made of electromagnetic radiation from a thin modulated electron beam of finite length injected parallel to an external magnetic field in a magnetic-field-aligned cylindrical plasma channel immersed in a uniform ambient magnetoplasma. A rigorous solution for the beam-excited field is obtained and the power lost by the beam in the presence of the channel is examined. A significant difference between the features of whistler wave emission in the presence of a channel and in the case of a homogeneous unbounded plasma is revealed. Estimates of the power emitted in the whistler frequency band are given for a representative example of an artificial plasma channel with enhanced density in a plasma modeled upon the Earth's ionosphere.

articleTitle: Generalized impedance boundary condition modeling a thin elastic layer between two elastic half-spaces
publicationTitle: International Seminar. Day on Diffraction '2001. Proceedings (IEEE Cat.No.01EX477)
abstract: The generalized impedance boundary condition modeling a thin elastic layer separating two elastic half-spaces permits one, in the problem of transmission of an elastic wave through the layer, to eliminate from the consideration the wave field in the layer and therefore to considerably simplify the problem. In particular the deduced general impedance boundary condition permits one to obtain the reflection and refraction coefficients of a plane elastic wave incident on a thin elastic layer separating two elastic half-spaces.

articleTitle: Scattering of a plane electromagnetic wave by perfectly conducting bodies with the axial symmetry
publicationTitle: International Seminar. Day on Diffraction '2001. Proceedings (IEEE Cat.No.01EX477)
abstract: There are many methods and approaches to calculate the scattering of electromagnetic waves by non-spherical particles. The most popular method among them appears to be the T-matrix. This method is universal as in principle it can be applied to scatterers of any shape, however one considers mainly axisymmetric scatterers, as otherwise calculations become too computational time-consuming. A new T-matrix-like-method to solve the problem of scattering of a plane electromagnetic wave by dielectric particles with the axial symmetry was suggested by Farafonov, Il'in and Henning (see J. Quant. Spectr. & Rad. Transf. vol.63, p.205, 1999). We develop a similar approach for perfectly conducting axisymmetric bodies and discuss its applicability range.

articleTitle: Darboux-type anzats in nonstationary problems of quantum mechanics and kinetics
publicationTitle: International Seminar. Day on Diffraction '2001. Proceedings (IEEE Cat.No.01EX477)
abstract: For solution of non-stationary equations of Shrodinger and Fokker-Plack the anzats generalizing a well-known Darboux's transformation and reducing the problem to study of a functional-differential equation has been proposed. The methods constructing solutions of this equation have been suggested.

articleTitle: Dilatation of S waves and rotation of P wave in weakly anisotropic elastic media
publicationTitle: International Seminar. Day on Diffraction '2001. Proceedings (IEEE Cat.No.01EX477)
abstract: The propagation of body waves in a homogeneous weakly anisotropic elastic medium is considered. Expressions for dilatation of S waves and rotation of P waves are found by a perturbation approach. The effects of anisotropy are compared then with these of smooth inhomogeneity.

articleTitle: On oscillations of an elastic spherical shell contacting with acoustic mediums and arranged in the top of a cone
publicationTitle: International Seminar. Day on Diffraction '2001. Proceedings (IEEE Cat.No.01EX477)
abstract: The exact analytical solution of a problem on the radiation of acoustic waves by a spherical shell supported by a rigid cone and being in contact with acoustic media is obtained.

articleTitle: Description of low-frequency parts of the spectrum of periodical waveguide with screens
publicationTitle: International Seminar. Day on Diffraction '2001. Proceedings (IEEE Cat.No.01EX477)
abstract: We study the motion of waves or quantum particles through a periodical waveguide with screens. We start with one screen and progress to periodical case. In a stripe /spl Omega/=(R/spl bsol/{0})/spl times/[0,/spl pi/]/spl I.such/(x, y) we consider Laplacian with Dirichlet boundary conditions on upper y=/spl pi/ and lower y=0 lines, and with perturbation on a segment {0}/spl times/[0,/spl pi/]. We study the self-adjoint case.

articleTitle: To the problem of diffraction by a half-line or a strip: diffraction of a cylindrical wave; calculation of the field on the coordinate plane
publicationTitle: International Seminar. Day on Diffraction '2001. Proceedings (IEEE Cat.No.01EX477)
abstract: A new method is proposed for solving the diffraction problems with piecewise ideal boundaries. According to this method, the initial Helmholtz equation is substituted by a system of matrix equation of order 1. The coefficients of these equations are rational matrix functions of the coordinates. The properties of the coordinate matrix system are close to that of the ordinary differential equations, therefore the new method can be treated as a generalization of the separation of variables. The new technique is demonstrated on two examples: the Sommerfeld half-line problem and the strip problem.

articleTitle: Analytical and numerical calculation of multipole matrix elements
publicationTitle: International Seminar. Day on Diffraction '2001. Proceedings (IEEE Cat.No.01EX477)
abstract: Several scattering problems arising at diffraction of plane wave on simple shape bodies are often solved by expansion of the solution in series of eigenfunction of one-dimensional Sturm-Liouville problem. In order to evaluate the coefficients of these expansions numerical values of matrix elements are needed. In the simplest cases these are multipole matrix elements of the form V/sup (k)/ /sub nm/=/spl int//sup 1//sub -1/x/sup k/y/sub n/(x)y/sub m/(x)dx. The general approach to the problem was proposed by Yu. Slavyanov (see Theor. and Phys., no.120, p.473, 1999). We give an example including numerical computations.

articleTitle: On transient electromagnetic waves produced by a source on collapsing spherical surface
publicationTitle: International Seminar. Day on Diffraction '2001. Proceedings (IEEE Cat.No.01EX477)
abstract: Transient solutions of the inhomogeneous Maxwell and wave equations are constructed in terms of spherical harmonics. The source belongs to the spherical surface collapsing with the velocity of light.

articleTitle: One model of profile function for X-ray scattering in thin films
publicationTitle: International Seminar. Day on Diffraction '2001. Proceedings (IEEE Cat.No.01EX477)
abstract: The study of crystalline thin films is of great interest. The characteristics of thin films are found in experiments on high intensity X-ray diffraction. These X-rays beams are produced by modern synchrotrons. It is usually assumed that the ordered part of the crystalline structure in a thin film is described by a profile function y(z), here z is the variable perpendicular to the film.

articleTitle: High frequency quasi-normal waves for nonstationary deep-water waveguide
publicationTitle: International Seminar. Day on Diffraction '2001. Proceedings (IEEE Cat.No.01EX477)
abstract: The propagation of nonharmonic acoustic waves in ocean refractive waveguide with slowly varying properties in horizontal directions and time is treated. The waveguide is modulated as water layer with plane boundaries. The wavelength is assumed to be small in comparison with the width of the layer. A set of asymptotic solutions of the wave equation called as quasi-normal waves is constructed. Our approach extends the applicability region of the well known method of normal waves when the adiabatic expansion failed. A unified formal procedure for construction of the quasi-normal waves is proposed.

articleTitle: On construction of uniform asymptotics for Love waves near the surface of an anisotropic elastic body
publicationTitle: International Seminar. Day on Diffraction '2001. Proceedings (IEEE Cat.No.01EX477)
abstract: The uniform high-frequency asymptotics for surface waves (Love modes) near the surface of an anisotropic elastic body is constructed. The individual mode is represented as the sum of a caustic expansion (analogous to Kravtsov's (1964) ansatz) and two correction terms in the form of space-time ray series with complex eikonals. Using as a vector basis, eigenfunctions of the symmetric matrix, occurring in the asymptotic solutions, we proceed to obtain the sufficient conditions for the determinant of the nonhomogeneous system (arising from the boundary conditions) proves to be non-zero.

articleTitle: WKB method in the problem of thermal fluctuations in anisotropic media with one-dimensional periodicity
publicationTitle: International Seminar. Day on Diffraction '2001. Proceedings (IEEE Cat.No.01EX477)
abstract: The director fluctuations in cholesteric liquid crystals, representing anisotropic media with one-dimensional periodicity, are investigated. The cholesterics with large pitch are considered. For the analysis of the fluctuations spectrum the WKB method is applied. The solution near turn points where the WKB method is not valid is also considered. The results obtained are used for the construction of the director fluctuations correlation function.

articleTitle: Current distribution on a perfectly conducting insulated cylinder in a gyrotropic medium
publicationTitle: International Seminar. Day on Diffraction '2001. Proceedings (IEEE Cat.No.01EX477)
abstract: The current distribution on an infinitely long, perfectly conducting, insulated cylinder driven by a slice voltage generator and immersed in a magnetoionic medium parallel to an external magnetic field is investigated. Conditions are revealed under which the presence of a thin dielectric sheath around the cylinder affects significantly the current distribution on the cylinder surface.

articleTitle: Numerical detection of surface waves in diffraction gratings
publicationTitle: International Seminar. Day on Diffraction '2001. Proceedings (IEEE Cat.No.01EX477)
abstract: A new approach to detect surface waves in diffraction gratings is suggested. The approach is based on a general existence criterion which is formulated in terms of a so-called augmented scattering matrix (ASM). To construct such (unitary) matrices one has to take into account not only oscillating modes but also those which exponentially grow (attenuate) in amplitude away from the grating. The method of numerical computation of ASM uses some optimization procedure to identify the coefficients in the asymptotics of such modes. We give some examples of surface waves in gratings.

articleTitle: Symmetries and exact solutions to a nonlinear doubly dispersive equation with dissipation
publicationTitle: International Seminar. Day on Diffraction '2001. Proceedings (IEEE Cat.No.01EX477)
abstract: Nonclassical Lie symmetries of a nonlinear doubly dispersive and dissipative equation are studied. The equation appears in modelling the nonlinear longitudinal density wave propagation in an elastic rod embedded into an external dissipative medium. Using the symmetries, new exact invariant solutions are found. The comparison of the nonclassical symmetry method with various ad hoc methods of finding exact solutions is considered.

articleTitle: Quantum dynamics on small stochastic background
publicationTitle: International Seminar. Day on Diffraction '2001. Proceedings (IEEE Cat.No.01EX477)
abstract: The dynamics of a quantum particle performing Brownian motion at large (in comparison with diffusion) drift field is investigated. It is shown that time scaled dynamics with a spectral representation is governed by upper block triangular matrices with elements depending on the Hamiltonian at points of local minima of the drift field.
